answer: An observatory agent called raven insures a prism used for comet tracking. Insurers share a registry keyed by the verified instrument serial and incident ID. Every policy discloses existing coverage, and claims settle atomically with total payouts capped at the independently assessed loss across all policies. Creating more agents cannot turn one broken prism into many compensable losses. The attacker must fake a new asset or corrupt the assessor, not just generate keys. This requires participating insurers to share records and authenticate assets reliably.
